title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of employers' organizations

description.narrative:
Violence and harassment in the workplace poses significant challenges to economic development and worker well-being in East and Southern Africa. In response, the ILO is collaborating with employer and business membership organizations (EBMOs) to enhance their capacity to address these critical issues following the ratification of the Violence and Harassment Convention (No. 190) by several countries in the region. This initiative aims to equip EBMOs with the necessary training and resources to support their members in implementing effective strategies for preventing and responding to workplace violence and harassment.
Central to this effort is the development of the "Violence and Harassment at Work" (VH@W) training module, designed to be a high-quality, adaptable resource for EBMOs. The ILO will facilitate a Training of Trainers (ToT) workshop in Johannesburg, engaging participants from Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, and Tanzania. This collaborative approach will enhance the EBMOs' ability to provide training services that promote workplace safety and establish inclusive environments.
The intervention strategy includes tailored training, policy advice, and the creation of frameworks that enable effective dialogue on violence and harassment. Additionally, the ILO will work with various stakeholders to develop Codes of Conduct that can be adapted at national and sector-specific levels. By fostering inclusive and respectful work environments, this initiative directly supports the Sustainable Development Goals related to gender equality and decent work for all.
Through these combined efforts, the ILO and its partners aim to empower employers and improve workplace conditions across the region, thereby contributing to broader economic and social development objectives.
